title: Security appliances software versions MX 26.1.6 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Generally Available MX Security & SD-WAN firmware is now available

Executive summary: MX 26.1.6 is a maintenance update for the MX 26.1 release family.
VPN fixes address dropped Auto VPN traffic, IPsec VPN recovery after WAN failover, and IKEv1 Client VPN connection setup.
Dashboard fixes correct stale cellular data, mislabeled WAN uplinks, missing IPv6 eBGP next hops, and inaccurate Summary Report utilization.
What's new: C8111-C-G2-MX and C8121-CW-G2-MX secure routers now allow the eSIM bootstrap cellular interface to come up when a wired uplink is connected.
Bug fixes - general fixes: Fixed an issue that could cause Cisco Secure Client VPN sessions to report an incorrect client IP address in event logs and RADIUS records. (MX-49995)
Fixed an issue that could drop return Auto VPN traffic on some MX appliances in passthrough mode with VPN NAT enabled. (MX-47834)
Corrected an issue that could drop Auto VPN traffic when a downstream peer connected through an upstream MX LAN subnet that was not enabled for VPN. (MX-50550)

Fixed an issue that could cause IPsec VPN traffic to stop after a WAN failover because the VPN tunnel did not reconnect through the active WAN uplink. This affected configurations using IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks. (MX-49987)
Resolved an issue that could prevent remote users from establishing new IKEv1 Client VPN connections when IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks was enabled. (MX-50879)
Resolved an issue that could cause Azure vMX instances with Accelerated Networking to restart unexpectedly when switching between routed and passthrough modes. (MX-49700)
Corrected an issue that could cause Dashboard to display an empty next hop for routes learned from link-local IPv6 eBGP peers. (MX-49629)
Fixed an issue that could stop DHCP services when a fixed IP assignment matched overlapping DHCP scopes. (MX-48442)
Fixed an issue that could cause Dashboard to show stale cellular network and radio information after the modem disconnected. (MX-48463)
Corrected an issue that could cause Dashboard's live uplink traffic graph to label a configured WAN uplink incorrectly on appliances using WAN Uplink Sharing. (MX-48468)
Resolved an issue that could cause Summary Report to show 0% device utilization or insufficient usage data on some appliances. (MX-49547)
Corrected an issue that could cause AMP cloud lookup errors to be reported in syslog as malicious file events when fail-close behavior blocked the download. (MX-46715)
Resolved an issue that could allow traffic to FQDNs removed from organization-wide group policy firewall rules until cached DNS entries expired. (MX-49341)
Fixed an issue that could cause appliances to restart unexpectedly while capturing packets on a WAN interface that was receiving IPv6 Router Advertisements. (MX-49678)
Corrected an issue that could prevent vMX appliances from downloading intrusion detection and prevention rules after startup. (MX-51218)
Bug fixes - limited platform fixes: Fixed an issue that could cause C8121-G2-MX secure routers to restart unexpectedly while processing some Auto VPN traffic. (MX-48837)
Corrected an issue that could leave 1 Gbps copper SFP ports without link after startup on C8355-G2-MX secure routers. (MX-49859)
Fixed an issue that could delay disabling SFP ports on C8455-G2-MX secure routers. (MX-44677)
Fixed an issue that could cause disabled WAN3 uplinks on MX75, MX85, MX95, and MX105 appliances to appear in Dashboard loss and latency history with 100% loss. (MX-47004)
Resolved an issue that could prevent 1 Gbps fiber links from establishing on MX95 and MX105 appliances when the connected device used auto-negotiation. (MX-51846)
Legacy products notice: When configured for this version, Z3(C) devices will run MX 19.2.8.
When configured for this version, MX64(W), MX65(W), MX84, MX100, and vMX100 devices will run MX 18.107.13.
Known issues: Networks configured with legacy IPv4 manual inbound firewall rules but no NAT Exceptions may have those rules hidden after upgrading to Wired 26.1.3 or later. Add a NAT Exception before making further configuration changes to avoid losing the rules. See NAT Exceptions documentation for more info.
On MX appliances in HA with a virtual IP, configuring an IPsec VPN peer to use multiple WAN uplinks may prevent all IPsec VPN tunnels from establishing. (MX-49849)
On MX 26.1 appliances, Auto VPN tunnels may fail to establish over WAN 3 when it is the only active uplink and a peer is running firmware earlier than MX 26.1. (MX-50123)
On MX appliances using VRFs other than the default VRF, IPv4 limited broadcast and multicast traffic may follow the default route instead of being discarded. (MX-52095)
When IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks is enabled, IKEv1 Client VPN connections may fail if upstream NAT changes the client's IKE source port from UDP 500. (MX-51712)
DNS resolution may fail for clients on a VLAN configured to use “Proxy upstream DNS” when the VLAN is bound to a Group Policy that denies traffic to the same VLAN subnet. (MX-47367)
Other: The product complies with EN 18031-1:2024 and EN 18031-2: 2024

Security appliances software versions MX 26.1.6 changelog

Executive summary

  • MX 26.1.6 is a maintenance update for the MX 26.1 release family.

  • VPN fixes address dropped Auto VPN traffic, IPsec VPN recovery after WAN failover, and IKEv1 Client VPN connection setup.

  • Dashboard fixes correct stale cellular data, mislabeled WAN uplinks, missing IPv6 eBGP next hops, and inaccurate Summary Report utilization.

What's new

  • C8111-C-G2-MX and C8121-CW-G2-MX secure routers now allow the eSIM bootstrap cellular interface to come up when a wired uplink is connected.

Bug fixes - general fixes

  • Fixed an issue that could cause Cisco Secure Client VPN sessions to report an incorrect client IP address in event logs and RADIUS records. (MX-49995)

  • Fixed an issue that could drop return Auto VPN traffic on some MX appliances in passthrough mode with VPN NAT enabled. (MX-47834)

  • Corrected an issue that could drop Auto VPN traffic when a downstream peer connected through an upstream MX LAN subnet that was not enabled for VPN. (MX-50550)

  • Fixed an issue that could cause IPsec VPN traffic to stop after a WAN failover because the VPN tunnel did not reconnect through the active WAN uplink. This affected configurations using IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks. (MX-49987)

  • Resolved an issue that could prevent remote users from establishing new IKEv1 Client VPN connections when IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks was enabled. (MX-50879)

  • Resolved an issue that could cause Azure vMX instances with Accelerated Networking to restart unexpectedly when switching between routed and passthrough modes. (MX-49700)

  • Corrected an issue that could cause Dashboard to display an empty next hop for routes learned from link-local IPv6 eBGP peers. (MX-49629)

  • Fixed an issue that could stop DHCP services when a fixed IP assignment matched overlapping DHCP scopes. (MX-48442)

  • Fixed an issue that could cause Dashboard to show stale cellular network and radio information after the modem disconnected. (MX-48463)

  • Corrected an issue that could cause Dashboard's live uplink traffic graph to label a configured WAN uplink incorrectly on appliances using WAN Uplink Sharing. (MX-48468)

  • Resolved an issue that could cause Summary Report to show 0% device utilization or insufficient usage data on some appliances. (MX-49547)

  • Corrected an issue that could cause AMP cloud lookup errors to be reported in syslog as malicious file events when fail-close behavior blocked the download. (MX-46715)

  • Resolved an issue that could allow traffic to FQDNs removed from organization-wide group policy firewall rules until cached DNS entries expired. (MX-49341)

  • Fixed an issue that could cause appliances to restart unexpectedly while capturing packets on a WAN interface that was receiving IPv6 Router Advertisements. (MX-49678)

  • Corrected an issue that could prevent vMX appliances from downloading intrusion detection and prevention rules after startup. (MX-51218)

Bug fixes - limited platform fixes

  • Fixed an issue that could cause C8121-G2-MX secure routers to restart unexpectedly while processing some Auto VPN traffic. (MX-48837)

  • Corrected an issue that could leave 1 Gbps copper SFP ports without link after startup on C8355-G2-MX secure routers. (MX-49859)

  • Fixed an issue that could delay disabling SFP ports on C8455-G2-MX secure routers. (MX-44677)

  • Fixed an issue that could cause disabled WAN3 uplinks on MX75, MX85, MX95, and MX105 appliances to appear in Dashboard loss and latency history with 100% loss. (MX-47004)

  • Resolved an issue that could prevent 1 Gbps fiber links from establishing on MX95 and MX105 appliances when the connected device used auto-negotiation. (MX-51846)

Legacy products notice

  • When configured for this version, Z3(C) devices will run MX 19.2.8.

  • When configured for this version, MX64(W), MX65(W), MX84, MX100, and vMX100 devices will run MX 18.107.13.

Known issues

  • Networks configured with legacy IPv4 manual inbound firewall rules but no NAT Exceptions may have those rules hidden after upgrading to Wired 26.1.3 or later. Add a NAT Exception before making further configuration changes to avoid losing the rules. See NAT Exceptions documentation for more info.

  • On MX appliances in HA with a virtual IP, configuring an IPsec VPN peer to use multiple WAN uplinks may prevent all IPsec VPN tunnels from establishing. (MX-49849)

  • On MX 26.1 appliances, Auto VPN tunnels may fail to establish over WAN 3 when it is the only active uplink and a peer is running firmware earlier than MX 26.1. (MX-50123)

  • On MX appliances using VRFs other than the default VRF, IPv4 limited broadcast and multicast traffic may follow the default route instead of being discarded. (MX-52095)

  • When IPsec VPN over multiple WAN uplinks is enabled, IKEv1 Client VPN connections may fail if upstream NAT changes the client's IKE source port from UDP 500. (MX-51712)

  • DNS resolution may fail for clients on a VLAN configured to use “Proxy upstream DNS” when the VLAN is bound to a Group Policy that denies traffic to the same VLAN subnet. (MX-47367)
